taxonomic_note: Accepted by current treatments. Modern Croton section Heptallon work recognizes infraspecific structure; this learner remains at species rank unless local material is confidently assigned below species.
look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST — THREE-SEED CROTON: low branched hairy Croton similar to prairie tea; its lower leaf surface does NOT look brown-dotted from dark-centered stellate hairs (the hairs are pale). On a clearly exposed PISTILLATE flower, count THREE BIFID styles with SIX terminal arms; its ovary is three-locular and mature capsule smooth. Existing Joey Santore licensed photos show true fine hairy leaf blades, green closed structures and WHITE MALE STAMENS, but the key 6 female tips and underside hair-center absence are NOT directly measurable. Confirm on multiple leaves and female flowers; do not mistake this for C. lindheimeri, the more robust woolly croton (distinct species).

project_inclusion.range_basis: A modern revision of Croton section Heptallon documents representative C. lindheimerianus var. lindheimerianus material from Llano (Enchanted Rock), Medina (near Devine), and Travis (Austin/Colorado River), all inside the project target zone.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Do not reuse the previously considered Williamson evidence for the project threshold; the locked three-county set is Llano, Medina, and Travis.

best_field_traits: lower leaf surface lacks the dark brown-dot effect of C. monanthogynus
pistillate sepals usually 5–6 and broadest toward their tips
three bifid styles yielding six terminal segments
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Croton monanthogynus has dark-centered stellate hairs that create a brown-dotted lower leaf surface, two styles/four terminal branches, and an effectively one-seeded fruit. Croton lindheimeri is generally more robust with much larger yellowish-woolly pistillate sepals.

comparisons.key_distinctions: No brown-dot effect beneath the leaves plus three bifid styles/six terminal branches separate C. lindheimerianus from C. monanthogynus; its smaller pistillate sepals help separate it from C. lindheimeri.

photo_diagnostic_lesson.title: Three-seed croton: inspect a female, not only the stamens

steps.what: Joey photographs are close shots of flower clusters and foliage; they do not establish whole mature habit.

steps.look: No dark brown hair centers below leaves
steps.what: Use a focused leaf UNDERSIDE macro beside confirmed prairie tea. The present images show pale fuzzy blades but NOT decisive absence of microscopic brown hair centers.

Find the female flower, take a high-magnification overhead photograph and count six free style segments. Joey images contain projecting MALE STAMENS and rounded structures but do not resolve a valid six-arm count.
Photograph ripe fruit laterally with 1mm ruler, distinguish from one-seeded prairie tea and warty dioecious Texas croton.

photo_diagnostic_lesson.memory_rule: LOW BUSH, NO BROWN DOTS + SIX FEMALE STYLE TIPS = THREE-SEED CROTON.

visual_comparison.title: Three-seed croton: white stamens, furry leaves, six-tip challenge
visual_comparison.subtitle: Two physically stored and individually licensed Joey Santore CC BY-NC 4.0 photos contain real useful flower/leaf evidence and SIX visible anatomy arrow markers. The older UT voucher photo remains an original restricted source record but is EXCLUDED from these public teaching panels. Six female style tips remain an actual missing macro.

items.label: 1 · Three-seed croton — Joey's flower & leaf macro
items.creator: Joey Santore
items.image_role: Real source-correct flower branch and densely hairy broad leaves; separate 6 styles not visible
items.caption: The broad leaf's pale star-hair texture, hairy stem, several small rounded buds/developing flowers and a WHITE STAMINATE flower with projecting stamens are visible. DO NOT label the nearby pale protrusions as six countable female style tips; they are overlapping.
items.why_it_matters: Shows micro-hair coverage and small sexual flower structures. Hair centers and true style count require greater resolution and right angle.

items.label: 2 · Three-seed croton — Joey's flowering nodes
items.creator: Joey Santore
items.image_role: Real source-correct paired-looking leaf cluster from SHORT close internodes, tiny clustered flowers and fuzzy axis
items.caption: Pale furry leaves crowd close to tiny pistillate/staminate flower structures. One green left leaf and one green right leaf can LOOK opposite because crowded at a branch node; Croton leaves are normally ALTERNATE. Neither star-hair dark centers nor six style-tip branches can be reliably counted here.
items.why_it_matters: Shows how crowded Croton inflorescence leaves can fool a novice into calling leaf arrangement opposite.

visual_comparison.memory_rule: THREE styles split once each → SIX female tips, not the stamens visible in some current photographs.
visual_comparison.annotation_status: Both CC BY-NC 4.0 Joey originals visually inspected, 6 true visible targets. The older photo with 'reuse rights unverified' stays out of annotated/public genus views. No false count of six style tips; mobile check pending.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Croton lindheimerianus — count the female styles
steps: Look at the actual dense pale hairs on elliptic leaves and clustered green reproductive bodies.
A flowering stem can show tiny WHITE projecting stamens; these are male reproductive parts, NOT female style branches.
Turn over a leaf with a lens; absence of dark brown-centered stellate hairs supports three-seed croton.
Use a FEMALE flower macro to count SIX style tips from THREE once-forked styles. Without the female head, keep Croton sp.
field_photo_quickcheck.field_rule: Six terminal female style tips + non-brown-dotted stellate hairs. Low branching annual by itself overlaps prairie tea.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: Do not use the existing UT voucher image in public photo lessons: its reuse permission is not verified. The two Joey images are CC BY-NC for noncommercial educational use only.
